devGlobal.text:
DEV NOTES · APPLIES EVERYWHERE

• Input model = WORD FIRST. The player types; the engine re-computes legal placements on every keystroke and the board shows the first one as a ghost. Rotate (or tap the ghost) cycles; tapping an anchor filters; Place / Enter commits.
• No timer, no timeouts, one mode.
• Walls: apart from the anchor, every cell of a new word must be empty. The only shared cells are anchors where two of the SAME player's words meet (mini glyph in the corner).
• Placements for a typed string: for each cell of your latest word whose letter = first letter → start there, across and down; whose letter = last letter → end there, across (going left) and down (going up). Keep only those where every other cell is in bounds and empty. First move: Blue starts on (1,1), Orange ends on (8,8).
• Deterministic order so "2 of 3" is stable: start-on-anchor before end-on-anchor, across before down, then anchor order along the word.
• Dictionary must be local (bundled list or trie): live feedback runs on every key press, no network round trip. Same list on the server for validation.
• Perspective: "You" = the local player. Pass-and-play recolours ghost, Place, entry and keyboard anchor keys from one active-player token (--p).
• Shape is identity: Blue tiles round, Orange tiles square + hatch. % radii so it holds at every size.
• Accessibility: entry row is role=textbox with the typed word; feedback line is role=status (polite). Meters are role=meter with text. Cells announce row, column, letter, owner. Respect prefers-reduced-motion (no shake: use the message alone).

devRules.text:
DECISIONS TO CONFIRM

• Danger meter: counts EXITS (letter of your latest word + direction with ≥2 empty cells: room for a 3-letter word). Cheap and visible. "Cornered" itself must come from the real dictionary check, not the meter.
• Live dictionary leaks: "Fits so far" vs "no fit yet" is geometry only, never dictionary, so the feedback can't be used to brute-force words letter by letter. Dictionary validity is only revealed as the green "fits" state or on Enter. Confirm this is acceptable.
• Hints: count per game (Off / 1 / 3), same for both players, shown in results. Should using a hint be visible to the opponent live?
• Resign available only on your own turn (mock), or any time?
• Collinear extension: can a word run straight on from the latest word's line? Mock assumes yes when the cells are empty.
• Adjacency: no Scrabble-style side-word check (mock assumes none).
• Rematch: who goes first? (Affects the 4-letter offset.)
• "A word already on the board can't be played again" includes the opponent's words (mock assumes yes).

dev01.text:
01 · YOUR TURN BEGINS

• Keyboard active, entry row empty with a blinking caret in slot 1. Anchors (cells of your latest word) pulse on the board.
• Keyboard hint: keys for your anchor letters (S T A R) get a tinted fill, a ring and a dot. That tells you what your word must start or end with, without giving an answer. Setting: "Highlight anchor keys".
• Opponent's last word flashes once (~2s) and the feedback line reads "Orange played BUS · start or end on S, T, A or R". (The mock loops the flash.)
• Rotate is disabled ("–"), Place looks inactive until something is ready.
• Status bar: both danger meters, turn number + chevron to the active player, cells in small muted text.

dev02a.text:
02a · TYPING · PARTIAL GHOST

• Each key press: append letter, recompute placements, reset to placement #1, redraw ghost (~30ms letter stagger, no exit animation).
• While the string is still a prefix (or ≥3 letters but not a real word yet), the ghost is PARTIAL: dotted grey outline, grey letters, the anchor gets a dotted ring. Entry tiles are neutral.
• Partial placements = words STARTING on an anchor, with room for at least 3 letters from there. End-on-anchor can't be known until the word is complete, so it appears once the last letter matches.
• Feedback: "Fits so far · 2 spots · keep typing". Rotate already works on partial ghosts.
• Max 5 letters (4 on Blue's first turn): extra key presses do nothing; slots past the cap are drawn dashed and faded.

dev02b.text:
02b · TYPING · NO FIT YET

• Shown when no placement exists for what's typed so far, e.g. "OP": O isn't an anchor letter, and an end-on-anchor fit can only appear once the word is complete (OPTS would end on S).
• Deliberately neutral: grey text, no icon, no shake, no red. It's not an error yet.
• Copy: "No fit yet · start or end on S, T, A or R".
• Never block typing because of this state; the player may be heading for an end-on-anchor word.

dev03.text:
03 · READY TO PLACE

• Ready = real word AND not already on the board AND ≥1 placement (after anchor filter).
• Ghost switches to the READY look: dashed outline in your colour, tinted fill, breathing; anchor cell gets a ring + link badge. Entry tiles fill with your tint; the anchor letter's tile gets a ring so you can see which letter is shared.
• Feedback (with check icon): "RAT fits · Rotate for 2 more spots".
• Place button becomes primary and reads "Place RAT". Enter does the same.
• On Place: tiles pop in (~60ms stagger), +n floats on your cells count, both meters recompute, entry clears, turn hands over.

dev04.text:
04 · ROTATE

• Rotate = index + 1, wrap N → 1. Triggers: the Rotate key on the action row, tapping any ghost cell, Tab or Space on desktop. Never a letter key.
• No double-tap: it would delay single taps on the board and is invisible. Rotate key + tap-the-ghost cover both thumbs-on-keyboard and eyes-on-board users.
• Counter lives inside the Rotate key ("2 of 3"), so it's where your thumb already is.
• Typing another letter resets to placement #1 (the set of placements changed).
• Rotate disabled when N < 2.

dev04b.text:
04b · ANCHOR FILTER

• Tap a pulsing anchor cell → only placements that use that cell. Here T: RAT can only end on T (going down), so 1 of 1.
• Filtered anchor: thick static ring; others dim.
• Works before typing too (acts like "placement first" light): tap T first, then type.
• If the filter leaves 0 placements for the typed word, show "No fit yet · …" and keep the filter; tap the anchor again to clear. Filter resets at end of turn and when the entry is cleared.

dev05a.text:
05a · NOT IN THE WORD LIST

• Errors only appear on Enter / Place tap, never while typing.
• Place looks inactive when not ready, but stays tappable (aria-disabled, not disabled) so tapping it explains why. Same for Enter on a hardware keyboard.
• Entry row does a Wordle-style shake (~450ms); tiles get a dashed outline. Feedback (info icon, no red): "RAX isn't in our word list. Try another?"
• Error clears on the next key press.
• The partial ghost can still show (RAX fits geometrically); it never turns into the ready look.

dev05b.text:
05b · ALREADY ON THE BOARD

• Check order on Enter: too short (<3) → already played → not a word → doesn't fit. First match wins, one message at a time.
• Copy: "BUS is already on the board. Each word plays once."
• Optional polish: briefly outline the existing BUS on the board so the player sees where it is.

dev05c.text:
05c · DOESN'T FIT

• A real, unplayed word with zero placements. TREES: from T there are only 4 cells down; ending on S there are only 4 cells up.
• Copy: "No room for TREES from S, T, A or R. Try a shorter word."
• Typed TREE did fit (partial ghost) before the 5th letter: the ghost disappears the moment it stops fitting, which is the early warning.
• Too short (2 letters + Enter): "Words need 3 to 5 letters."

dev06.text:
06 · OPPONENT'S TURN

• Entry row becomes "Orange is typing…" (online: don't stream their letters). Keyboard faded and inert; Rotate/Place inactive; Resign disabled.
• Board read-only, meters current. Feedback line: "You played RAT · +2 cells".
• Hardware keyboard input is ignored on desktop while waiting (don't buffer letters into your next turn).
• No timer: decide an online idle policy separately.

devMain.text:
PLAY · PROTOTYPE

• Tweaks jump to any scene, theme or layout.
• Live: tap keys to type (small built-in word list), watch the partial → ready ghost, Rotate, tap the ghost, tap anchors, Place (meters update), Enter on invalid words for the messages, Resign, hint, tutorial.
• Not live: physical keyboard (canvas blocks global key handlers).

dev07a.text:
07a · YOU'RE IN DANGER

• Trigger: at turn start your room is 1 (2 = tight, quieter).
• Your chip pulses (outline, no colour change), meter gets hazard stripes + warning icon + "1 way out". No red.
• Escape route: with room ≤ 2 and the entry empty, the empty cells of each remaining exit get a dotted fill. Hidden as soon as you type (the ghost takes over). Setting: "Show escape routes".
• Feedback: "Only 1 way out left. Follow the dots."
• Haptic warning + polite screen-reader announcement when it first drops to 1.

dev07b.text:
07b · YOUR OPPONENT IS IN DANGER

• Same moment as 07a on Orange's device. Blue's chip shows the same danger treatment.
• Typing indicator says it: "Blue is down to 1 way out · typing…"
• Don't show Blue's escape-route dots on Orange's device.

dev08.text:
08 · CORNERED

• Checked automatically at the START of the player's turn: no dictionary word fits from any letter of their latest word → immediate loss. The keyboard never appears.
• Visuals computed from the board: sealed word (heavy outline, short shake), walls that stop each exit (heavy outline + crosshatch, any owner), gaps too short for 3 letters (dotted). Board edges count but aren't drawn.
• Hold until "See result" (or ~3s), then 11a.
• A gap can be geometrically long enough with no dictionary word that fits it: still cornered. Draw those exits as gaps too.

dev09a.text:
09a · RESIGN

• Flag icon in the header: out of the thumb zone, away from Place, always confirmed.
• Sheet: "Resign this game?" + reassurance that a fitting word exists (you'd already have lost otherwise). If hints are on, a hint offer sits above the buttons as the gentler option.
• Buttons: Keep playing (left, safe) · Resign (right, high-contrast neutral, not red).
• Resign → game over "You resigned · Orange wins". Log it as the end reason.
• Tapping the scrim = Keep playing.

dev09b.text:
09b · HINT

• Hint button (bulb) on the action row only when hints are enabled. Also offered from the Resign sheet.
• A hint = engine picks one legal word (prefer one that leaves room) and reveals ONE letter plus its length and the anchor letter: chip "F _ R · 2 left". It never types for you and never places.
• Reveal a letter that isn't the anchor (the anchor is already known).
• The chip stays until you place. Using another hint reveals a letter of the same word.
• Count decrements per game; 0 left → bulb disabled with "No hints left".

dev09c.text:
09c · SETTINGS (MENU)

• Hints per game: Off / 1 / 3. Default Off for ranked/online, 3 for casual vs bot (decide). Both players get the same count; the setting is per match, agreed before start online.
• Highlight anchor keys: default on.
• Show escape routes: default on.
• Settings open from the menu; in-match changes to hints are locked once the match starts (online).

dev10a.text:
10a · FIRST MOVE · BLUE

• Anchor = the empty corner (1,1), pulsing with START. The word must start there, across or down: 2 placements for every word.
• Max 4 letters: entry shows 4 live slots + a faded 5th; the 5th key press is ignored. Note above the entry: "First word: up to 4 letters, starting in the corner". Show it on this turn only.
• No anchor keys highlighted (any first letter works).
• Orange's corner shows a faint dashed END preview; hide once Blue places.

dev10b.text:
10b · FIRST MOVE · ORANGE

• Orange's word must END on (8,8): placements = across ending in column 8, down ending in row 8. Any 3–5 letters.
• Because the anchor is the last letter, the ghost can appear from the first letter typed (the end cell is fixed). Mock shows STONE ready, 1 of 2.
• Pass-and-play: everything recolours to orange. Online: only on Orange's device.

dev11a.text:
11a · GAME OVER · CORNERED

• Headline from the viewer's side: "Orange cornered you" / "You cornered Orange". Sub: turn + sealed word. Variant for resign: "You resigned".
• Board keeps the sealed word + walls. Loser's meter "No way out"; winner "—".
• Stats are secondary: words played, cells.
• Replay needs the move log {word, row, col, dir, player, turn} + end reason (cornered / resigned / full).

dev11b.text:
11b · GAME OVER · FULL BOARD (RARE)

• Grid full before anyone is cornered: more cells wins; tie → Orange (Blue moved first). Say why when the tie rule decides it.
• Only screen where cells are the headline. Meters "—".
• Mock board is a placeholder fill, not a played game.
• Check "grid full" right after each placement, before the next cornered check.

devMenu.text:
MAIN MENU

• First launch (no games played, tutorial not seen): Learn to play is the primary button with a "Start here" pill; New game is secondary. No modal: the order does the offering, and nobody is blocked from jumping straight in.
• Returning with a saved game: Continue first (shows turn, whose move, and the mover's danger level), New game primary, Learn to play as a small dashed row with "2 min".
• Returning without a saved game: same as returning, minus Continue.
• New game = pass and play for now. Subtitle and the footer line ("More opponents coming soon") leave room: later, New game opens a chooser (pass and play / vs computer / online). Don't add a picker until there's more than one option.
• Hero board: a looping animation of the two chains racing (cells pop in order, hold, fade, restart every ~9s). Decorative: aria-hidden, paused under reduced motion (show the final frame).
• Settings is a small gear top-right: theme (Auto/Light/Dark), hints per game, anchor-key highlight.

devMenu2.text:
MENU · STATE & PERSISTENCE

• "Seen tutorial" flag: set when the player finishes OR skips. First-launch layout only while unset and no game has been played.
• Continue restores the full game (board, move log, whose turn, hints left). One saved game slot is enough for pass and play.
• Starting a New game while one is saved: confirm "Abandon the game in progress?"

devLearn1.text:
LEARN TO PLAY · HOW IT WORKS

• It is the real game screen (same board, keyboard, ghost, Rotate, Place, placement engine) driven by a script of 9 steps. Only the header (Skip · progress dots · n/9) and the coach bar replace the status bar.
• Each typing step has a scripted word and a scripted placement. The engine still computes all legal placements; Place only enables when the ghost is on the scripted one (step 4: MAP must be rotated down first).
• Spotlight: cells that matter (anchors, ghost, the opponent's new word, walls) stay bright, everything else drops to ~28% opacity. On the keyboard, the next scripted letter is lifted and filled; all other keys dim but still work.
• Off-script typing is never an error: the letters stay, the feedback becomes a dashed pill "For this lesson, try TEAM · tap ⌫ to fix", and the spotlight moves to Backspace. If it's a real word, say so ("TOAD is a real word!").
• Opponent steps (3, 5): keyboard inert, the word pops in letter by letter (~120ms each) with the opponent flash, then a "Your turn" button. Don't auto-advance: the player reads at their own pace.
• Under 2 minutes: 4 words to type, 2 to watch, 1 bump, 1 win.

devLearn2.text:
LEARN TO PLAY · STEPS 6–9

• 6: TOP has no ghost until the last letter (end-on-anchor fits only appear when the word is complete). That's a useful moment: the coach line already says "END on your letter".
• 7: the ghost is FORCED across from O (see red note). Typing O-P already shows the P cell bumping; at the full word the entry shakes and the coach explains. "Got it" continues. Nothing is placed.
• 8: new position loads (fade the board, don't animate a whole game). Coach shows both meters; Orange reads "63 possible moves". After Place: POPE pops in, Orange's meter drops to "No moves left" (animate the number), JAIL gets the sealed outline, the walls and dead gaps light up, then "Finish".
• 9: recap of the 3 rules + Play now (starts a pass-and-play game) / Back to menu.
• Skip (any step except 9): confirm sheet; Skip goes to the menu and marks the tutorial as seen. Back on the menu, Learn to play always restarts from step 1.

devLearnRed.text:
SCRIPT CHECKS (for the brief owner)

• Step 7: OPEN does fit DOWN from the O of TOP (column 3, rows 4–6 are empty). In the real game typing OPEN would show a legal ghost, not a shake. The tutorial forces the across attempt so the lesson works. If you want it to be honest in-engine, use a word with no legal spot, e.g. one that's too long for every exit, or pre-block column 3.
• Step 8: "63 → 0 moves" counts real dictionary placements. The game screens' meter counts geometric exits; by that measure JAIL would still show 1 (the 4 empty cells left of J), because only the dictionary rules out words ending in J. Either switch the in-game meter to dictionary moves (recommended now that the tutorial teaches that number) or change step 8's copy to exits.
• All other steps check out with the placement engine: TEAM across from the corner; DOG down to (8,8); MAP across = placement 1, down = 2 of 2; BIG ends on G; TOP ends on P (1 of 1); POPE across from P is placement 1 of 4.

devDesk.text:
DESKTOP

• ≥1080px: three columns (players + meters | board | entry, keyboard, actions). Below that it stacks like mobile.
• Physical keyboard types: A–Z letters, Backspace deletes, Enter places (or explains why not), Tab or Space rotates, Esc clears the anchor filter then the entry. Ignore keys while a sheet/modal or a text field has focus, and while it's not your turn.
• Preventing default on Tab is required (focus would move). Keep a visible "Tab · rotate" hint so keyboard users aren't surprised, and keep focus management sane for screen-reader users (Rotate is also a real button).
• On-screen keyboard stays visible and clickable for mouse users, smaller keys (40px).
• Key caps on buttons only for fine pointers.
